message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data on the current air quality in Los Angeles. For the most up‑to‑date information you can check one of the following resources:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the latest AQI and pollutant levels. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles,” and see the live AQI, forecast, and historical trends. |
| **Local news sites** | Many local news outlets (e.g., LA Times, KABC) publish daily air‑quality updates. |
| **Mobile apps** | Apps like “AirVisual,” “Plume Labs: Air Report,” or “EPA AirNow” provide real‑time readings and alerts. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also use voice assistants (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask, “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They typically pull from the same data feeds.
